newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Faulding says no budget impact on profits.
newsitem.headline: Faulding says no budget impact on profits.

text.p: Pharmaceutical group F.H Faulding and Co Ltd said the federal government's plans to tighten spending on the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) was not expected to have a significant impact on the company's bottom line.

"I do not think it will have a significant effect at all," chief financial officer Peter Maloney told Reuters, saying the move was aimed at branded drug products while Faulding produced mostly generic equivalents.

"It will obviously affect to some extent producers of branded products," he said, adding there could also be some impact on the drug supply chain, such as pharmacists who might experience margin cuts.

The government announced in its 1997/98 budget handed down on Tuesday night that it would introduce a base price scheme for similar drugs, whereby any patient who chooses a more expensive drug than the base price drug will pay the difference.
The government also expects to make savings through the deletion from the PBS schedule of a number of drugs used to treat less serious medical conditions.

Maloney said the budget move was part of a drive by governments around the world to reduce the margin between the cost of production of drugs and the cost of delivering those drugs to the final consumer.
"This trend is consistent with what is happening in other markets, particularly in the United States, to encourage people to use the generic equivalents," he said.
